title: Microgel-Extracellular Matrix Composite Support for the Embedded 3D Printing of Human Neural Constructs
protocol: Prepare cell growth medium by adding supplements to DMEM/F12 with L-alanyl-L-glutamine dipeptide.
Stir vigorously for 4 hours at 60°C to prepare a 1% w/v alginate solution in ultrapure water.
Sterile-filter the dissolved, hot alginate solution using a 0.45 µm pore-size filter.
Store the filtered alginate solution at 4°C.
Prepare a 37 g/L NaHCO3 solution in ultrapure water.
Adjust the pH of the NaHCO3 solution to 9.5 with NaOH.
Filter-sterilize the adjusted pH solution and store it at 4°C.
Prepare a 2 mg/mL CaCO3 solution in ultrapure water in a sterile beaker.
Mix the CaCO3 solution 1:1 with the alginate solution.
Stir the mixture for 1 hour at room temperature using a magnetic stirrer.
Add acetic acid to the mixture in a 1:500 ratio.
Leave stirring overnight at 650 rpm.
Stir the alginate solution using a stirring magnet.
Fragment the gelled alginate solution into microparticles by homogenizing it at 15,000 rpm for 10 min.
Centrifuge the microparticles at 18,500 × g for 20 min at room temperature.
Discard the supernatant inside the LAF bench.
Resuspend the particles in DMEM containing 2 mM NaOH and 1% P/S.
Incubate overnight at 4 °C.
Add NaOH dropwise to turn the suspension red, if necessary.
Homogenize the particles at 15,000 rpm for 3 min.
Centrifuge at 18,500 × g for 10 min at room temperature.
Remove the supernatant carefully.
Store the alginate microparticle pellet at 4 °C until further use.
Resuspend the alginate microparticle pellet in twice the volume of growth medium containing 4% HEPES and 4% NaHCO3.
Incubate the resuspended microparticles overnight at room temperature.
Centrifuge the microgel suspension at 18,500 × g for 10 min at room temperature.
Discard the supernatant after centrifugation.
Dilute the collagen stock solution to reach a final concentration of 1 mg/mL.
Neutralize the diluted collagen by adding 4% HEPES and 4% NaHCO3.
Mix alginate microparticles with neutralized collagen in a 2:1 ratio on ice.
Pipette the mixture slowly up and down on ice to mix thoroughly.
Transfer the generated composite material into a cooled microwell plate or suitable printing container.
Use the SHAPE composite within 30 min.
Culture cells in a basement membrane extract-coated T75 flask in growth medium.
Passage cells at least two times after thawing before using them for the 3D printing experiment.
Dissociate cells enzymatically using a 0.025% trypsin solution for 5 min at 37 °C.
Neutralize trypsin with growth medium.
Centrifuge cell suspension at 400 × g for 5 min at room temperature.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 2-3 mL of growth medium.
Perform a cell count.
Centrifuge cells at 400 × g.
Resuspend the pellet in growth medium supplemented with 0.1% xanthan gum to prevent sedimentation, achieving a final concentration of 9 × 10^6 cells/mL.
Load 100 µL of tightly packed alginate microparticles into a syringe using a 21 G blunt metal needle.
Load the prepared cell suspension into the syringe using the same needle.
Replace the loading needle with a 27 G blunt metal needle for printing.
Design a structure using the referenced software.
Adjust the initial height of the printed structure within the depth of the SHAPE composite support.
Generate a G-Code by clicking on Generate.
Insert the cell-laden glass syringe into a volumetric extrusion head on an extrusion-based bioprinter.
Measure the needle length of the cell-laden glass syringe by clicking on Needle Length Measurement.
Place the microwell plate or container loaded with the SHAPE composite onto the printer.
Keep the cell plate or container at 4 °C until printing to prevent premature crosslinking of the support.
Measure the surface height of an empty well within the same microwell plate or container by clicking on SHM.
Alternatively, determine the surface height manually by measuring the height of the well with the needle.
Set the extrusion rate to 3.6 µL/min and the feed rate to 0.3 mm/s.
Test the extrusion before printing.
Pre-extrude a small volume to avoid nozzle clogging due to cell sedimentation.
Add a retraction volume to the volumetric syringe if necessary.
Keep the feed rate below 0.5 mm/s when inserting or exiting the SHAPE gel.
Load the G-Code into the printer's user interface.
Generate a new G-Code whenever changes are made to the designed structure.
Initiate the print procedure by clicking on Run.
Place the SHAPE gel at 37 °C in a cell culture incubator for 30 min after printing.
Add growth medium gently on top of the annealed SHAPE gel support.
Replace the growth medium with differentiation medium the next day.

Formulate differentiation medium using DMEM/F12 with L-alanyl-L-glutamine dipeptide, containing 30 mM glucose, 5 µM HEPES, 0.5% w/v lipid-rich bovine serum albumin, 40 µM each of L-alanine, L-asparagine monohydrate, L-aspartic acid, L-glutamic acid, and L-proline, 1% N2 supplement, 1% penicillin-streptomycin, 100 µM dibutyryl-cAMP, and 2 ng/mL glial cell-line derived neurotrophic factor (GDNF).
Tilt the plate and remove old medium gently without damaging the hydrogel.
Add fresh medium dropwise along the well wall containing the gel.
Refresh differentiation medium every 2 days until endpoint.
Remove excess medium from the gel for live-cell fluorescence imaging.
Add an equal volume of 20 μM Calcein AM (diluted in differentiation medium) to the support gel.
Incubate for 40 min at 37°C.
Remove Calcein AM solution and add fresh differentiation medium.
Transfer plate to microscope for imaging.
Remove excess medium from the gel for immunocytochemistry.
Transfer the gel to a larger container containing DPBS using a small spatula.
Wash the gel three times with DPBS for 20 min each time in a fume hood.
Add enough 4% formaldehyde solution to cover the gel and incubate for 1 h at room temperature.
Wash the gel three times with DPBS for 20 min each time.
Prepare blocking solution consisting of 5% donkey serum, 0.25% detergent, and 0.02% sodium azide in DPBS.
After washing with DPBS, add the blocking solution to the gel.
Incubate for 6 h at room temperature to prevent unspecific binding.
Rock the plate gently.
Prepare the primary antibody solution by diluting the TUBB3 antibody in blocking solution at a ratio of 1:1,000.
Remove the blocking solution from the gel.
Add the primary antibody solution and incubate for 48 h at 4 °C.
Rock the plate gently.
Wash three times with DPBS for 20 min each time.
Prepare the secondary antibody solution by diluting DAPI (1:1,000) and the secondary antibody (1:200) in blocking solution.
After washing with DPBS, incubate the gel in the secondary antibody solution for 24 h at 4 °C.
Rock the plate gently.
Wash three times with DPBS for 20 min each time.
Store at 4 °C until imaging.
Before imaging, transfer the stained gel with a spatula to a dish or a well-plate with a thin imaging bottom.
